answer.rationale:
The urgent pull is toward promotional_pricing, since memory_73 speaks directly to price-sensitive SMB. But memory_73 is a consolidated summary whose source I have not recovered this cycle, and my verification budget is spent — so I would be matching a deep competitor price cut with an unverified claim, under exactly the conditions (panic, deadline) where an over-general memory is most likely to be trusted uncritically. Discounting into a price war also carries the largest downstream value risk of any candidate: it anchors SMB expectations lower, erodes margin on the existing base, and tends to buy revenue that is not sustainable — which conflicts with the stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than a one-quarter save.

The only two claims I actually re-grounded this cycle are exp_86 and exp_31. exp_86 (shortened onboarding: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) is the single verified lever that moves retention in the right direction, and retention is the actual mechanism by which price-driven churn is lost. Faster time-to-value is also the honest counter to a cheaper competitor: it raises realized value rather than lowering price. exp_31 is verified but weaker for this purpose — its retention delta is -1%, and it is explicitly stated not to replicate outside SMB, so I am not treating it as license to change signup broadly.

Scale is standard_experiment, not broad rollout: exp_86 was observed on self-serve accounts, and I have no verified read on whether the effect size holds for the specific price-sensitive cohort now churning. Holding to a measured rollout preserves the ability to detect that.

Explicit residual uncertainty I am not papering over: (1) this action does not directly answer the price cut, and if the churn is genuinely price-elastic rather than value-driven, onboarding improvements will be too slow — that is a real cost of my choice, not a hidden one; (2) memory_73 may well be correct, and I am declining it on provenance, not on evidence against it; (3) memory_57, memory_91 and memory_44 are similarly unverified and should not be leaned on this cycle either. First priority next week is recovering the exp_73 source, plus a read on whether the current churn conversations cite price alone or price relative to value received — that determines whether a guarded, time-boxed, non-anchoring pricing response is warranted rather than an open discount.
